landmark_cases.title: Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington v. United States Department of Justice
landmark_cases.reason: Defines Exemption 7(A)’s requirement that enforcement proceedings be pending or reasonably anticipated and explains that the agency may establish ongoing investigations by attesting to their existence, while cautioning against vague assertions.

landmark_cases.title: Center for National Security Studies v. U.S. Department of Justice
landmark_cases.reason: Seminal D.C. Circuit authority on deference to the executive in FOIA cases implicating national security, including counterterrorism matters, and endorses the ‘tip-off’ interference rationale under Exemption 7(A).

landmark_cases.title: Silvia Patricia Miranda Juarez v. Department of Justice, Drug Enforcement Administration
landmark_cases.reason: Articulates that Exemption 7(A) applies so long as an investigation continues to gather evidence for a possible future case and that premature release could jeopardize it; also supports withholding whole documents when nonexempt material is inextricably intertwined.

landmark_cases.title: Pratt v. Webster
landmark_cases.reason: Establishes the ‘rational nexus’ test for the Exemption 7 threshold that records be compiled for law enforcement purposes, a foundational standard repeatedly applied in FBI FOIA cases.

landmark_cases.title: Campbell v. United States Department of Justice
landmark_cases.reason: Applies and reinforces the Pratt ‘rational nexus’ requirement and recognizes deference to the FBI’s law-enforcement judgments when invoking Exemption 7.

landmark_cases.title: Mead Data Central, Inc. v. U.S. Department of the Air Force
landmark_cases.reason: Foundational FOIA segregability precedent: agencies must release any reasonably segregable, meaningful information and may withhold when nonexempt material is interspersed and not reasonably segregable.
